newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK FARMERS TO BE COMPENSATED FOR BAD WEATHER.
newsitem.headline: GREEK FARMERS TO BE COMPENSATED FOR BAD WEATHER.

text.p: Greek Agriculture Minister Stephanos Tzoumakas said that the European Union had agreed to pay 10 billion drachmas in damages to farmers who lost crops to bad weather.
Greek farmers have been blockading Greek roads for 21 days, demanding higher subsidies and produce prices, lower petrol costs and taxes.
Tzoumakas said that the EU had rejected requests for subsidising farmers' incomes but agreed to allow the transfer of funds earmarked for agricultural infrastructure to pay for damaged crops.
"Since the mobilisations began, we told the unions and the public that we would bring up the issue of damages due to weather," he told a news conference.
He made clear this would be the only compensation given, saying no country was entitled to additional funds unless it had suffered a national disaster.
His ministry would cooperate with the national economy ministry to submit petitions to the EU by January 6 and the subsidies would be paid in early 1997, he added.
Farmers will be compensated for damages to crops, especially cotton, corn and wheat as well as losses in animal stock and farming installations, he said.
Farmers, especially cotton growers in the central Greek region of Thessaly, and the northern regions of Macedonia and Thrace have been especially hard-hit by storms.
He urged farmers to submit petitions for compensations, saying that out of a total of 46,953 cotton producers in six prefectures only 1,033 had applied for help.
Tzoumakas also said he had called for a meeting of the newly-appointed Agricultural Policy Council for January 10-11.

"Prime Minister Costas Simitis will inaugurate the session. Political parties and other bodies will be called to express their views," he said. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
